items.stem: A positive test charge is released from rest in a uniform electric field. How does it move?

options.text: It accelerates in the direction of the field
options.rationale: Correct: force on a positive charge is qE, along the field, producing acceleration.

options.text: It moves at constant velocity along the field
options.rationale: A constant force produces acceleration, not constant velocity.

options.text: It moves opposite to the field
options.rationale: A positive charge feels a force along the field, not against it.

options.text: It stays at rest because fields do no work at rest
options.rationale: The field exerts a force that sets the charge in motion.

items.explanation: Correct: force on a positive charge is qE, along the field, producing acceleration.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about Gauss's law are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The net flux through a closed surface depends only on the enclosed charge
options.rationale: Correct: flux is proportional to enclosed charge, by Gauss's law.

options.text: It is only useful for computing fields when the charge distribution has high symmetry
options.rationale: Correct: extracting the field from the flux integral requires symmetry.

options.text: It states that magnetic flux through any closed surface is nonzero
options.rationale: That describes magnetism; Gauss's law for electricity concerns electric charge.

options.text: It requires the surface to be a physical conductor
options.rationale: The Gaussian surface is an imaginary mathematical surface.

items.explanation: Correct: flux is proportional to enclosed charge, by Gauss's law.

items.stem: A bar magnet is pushed north-pole-first toward a conducting loop. By Lenz's law, the induced current in the loop will

options.text: flow so as to oppose the increase in flux, repelling the magnet
options.rationale: Correct: the induced current opposes the change, creating a repulsive force.

options.text: flow so as to attract the magnet faster
options.rationale: That would violate energy conservation; the force opposes the motion.

options.text: be zero because the magnet is a permanent magnet
options.rationale: A changing flux induces a current regardless of the field source.
The direction is fixed while the flux increases.

items.explanation: Correct: the induced current opposes the change, creating a repulsive force.
